      </g>
    </svg>
    </div>
    <figcaption><strong>One write door, one-way reads.</strong> Mutation exists only through the contract plane; projections derive from frozen snapshots and cannot write back; live state re-enters Canon only as <span class="mono">observed</span> records that carry a mandatory expiry.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <div class="law"><p>Read and reveal capabilities are structurally separated from write capabilities. A projection that writes back is a coupling wearing a projection’s clothes.</p><span class="who">ICP §4.5 · Fundamental’s projection purity contract</span></div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 3 ============================ -->
<section id="s3">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">3</span><h2>The record model</h2></div>

  <h3>3.1 <span class="sub">·</span> One envelope, five body kinds</h3>
  <p>Every record is a versioned envelope in the rr-rsp shape:</p>
  <pre>Envelope {
  schema_version      <span class="c">// wire protocol version, e.g. "scms-0.1"</span>
  subject_id          <span class="c">// stable identity, chosen by the owning authority</span>
  compatibility       <span class="c">// { protocol, subject_schema } — checked independently of identity</span>
  provenance          <span class="c">// { kind, authority, source, source_hash, observed_at?, expires_at? }</span>
  minimum_access      <span class="c">// access floor for the whole record</span>
  body                <span class="c">// tagged: Schema | Content | Relation | Observation | Topology</span>
}</pre>
  <p>Content types, themes, and contract definitions (<code>Schema</code>), documents (<code>Content</code>), typed edges (<code>Relation</code>), measurements and presence (<code>Observation</code>), and the delivery graph (<code>Topology</code>) are peers in one store, differentiated by tag — uniform identity, access projection, and provenance for all of them.</p>

  <h3>3.2 <span class="sub">·</span> Provenance is a four-class lattice</h3>
  <div class="prov-grid">
    <div class="prov"><span class="name">declared</span><p>Asserted by the authority that owns it. <strong>An author’s text, an editor’s confidence rating.</strong></p></div>
    <div class="prov"><span class="name">derived</span><p>Mechanically projected from an identified source. <strong>A rendered page, an index, a summary.</strong></p></div>
    <div class="prov"><span class="name">observed</span><p>Measured from a running system, time-bounded. <strong>Presence, delivery state, engagement.</strong> Must carry <span class="name">observed_at + expires_at</span>.</p></div>
    <div class="prov"><span class="name">system-certified</span><p>Emitted by an identified trusted pipeline from validated inputs. <strong>Resolver output with its trace.</strong></p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="law"><p>Consumers must not promote one provenance class into another. An observed engagement spike does not become declared importance; a derived summary does not become authored text.</p><span class="who">rr-rsp descriptor protocol</span></div>
  <p>Expiry governs <em>authority to decide</em>, not deletion — expired observations are retained for replay, but may no longer drive current-state decisions.</p>

  <h3>3.3 <span class="sub">·</span> Four identity classes, never conflated</h3>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Class</th><th>Stability contract</th><th>CMS instance</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Process-local</td><td>one session</td><td>editing session id, subscription id</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Build-local</td><td>one artifact</td><td>revision hash <span class="mono">(JCS → SHA-256)</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Schema key</td><td>stable across declared-compatible releases</td><td>content id, semantic slug namespace</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Human name</td><td>display only — no uniqueness</td><td>title, byline</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <p>A semantic replacement gets a <strong>new id</strong>; an editorial correction keeps the id. The content hash answers “same bytes”; compatibility answers “may be exchanged.” Different questions, checked by different mechanisms.</p>

  <h3>3.4 <span class="sub">·</span> Append-only, enforced by grants</h3>
  <p>Revision and receipt tables carry <strong>no UPDATE grant</strong> — custody lives in the database, not in convention (PDP’s pattern). There is no destructive edit and no destructive delete, only:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Supersession</strong> — a new revision names what it supersedes; the old becomes historical-only.</li>
    <li><strong>Revocation</strong> — prevents new use; retains all provenance needed to explain past use.</li>
    <li><strong>Entitlement hiding</strong> — content participates in discovery as a <em>protected resource</em>: geometry, relations, and metrics visible; the text layer gated.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>The receipt chain is hash-linked. Negative results — failed qualifications, rejected candidates, discredited metrics — are permanent project memory: never deleted, renumbered, or rewritten.</p>

  <h3>3.5 <span class="sub">·</span> Multi-axis state — the one-enum <code>status</code> field is prohibited</h3>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Axis</th><th>Values</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Semantic maturity</td><td class="mono">draft → complete → superseded</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Evidence state</td><td class="mono">unqualified → qualified → stale → invalidated</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Publication state</td><td class="mono">unpublished → promoted → embargoed → superseded → revoked</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Delivery state</td><td class="mono">unpropagated → propagating → synchronized → drifted</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <p>The axes are orthogonal: a document can be semantically complete, evidence-stale, still promoted, and drifted at one edge — and each of those facts matters separately. Likewise, absence vocabulary never collapses: <code>hidden ≠ unavailable ≠ absent ≠ unknown ≠ unsupported ≠ missing</code>. A renderer that merges any two of them has changed the reader’s understanding without computing anything.</p>

  <h3>3.6 <span class="sub">·</span> Relations associate; patterns couple</h3>
  <p>Typed edges (<code>supports</code>, <code>contradicts</code>, <code>precedes</code>, <code>part-of</code>, <code>adapts</code>, <code>references</code>, <code>same-creator</code>…) are <strong>non-causal by default</strong>. An edge moves nothing — no feed reordering, no emphasis change — until a named field pattern explicitly turns the association into a coupling, declared in the pattern’s passport. This guardrail keeps the system semantic and authorable rather than haunted.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 4 ============================ -->
<section id="s4">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">4</span><h2>Content types</h2></div>
  <p>The content type system is SES’s semantic model, mapped onto CMS vocabulary:</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>SES primitive</th><th>CMS meaning</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Element</td><td>Smallest meaningful unit (heading, image, button). Owns semantics and accessibility; minimal visual identity.</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Slot</td><td>A <strong>field</strong>: named, typed content participation inside a block (<code>title</code>, <code>media</code>, <code>meta</code>, <code>actions</code>…).</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Block</td><td>A content component (article section, media card, hero) — a semantic composition of elements and slots.</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Socket</td><td>A <strong>region with an admission policy</strong>: which blocks, what cardinality, what importance, which operations required.</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Composition</td><td>A <strong>page type</strong>: semantic arrangement of sockets — hierarchy and participation, not pixel layout.</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Variant · State</td><td>Semantic specialization (<code>primary</code>, <code>quiet</code>) · condition (<code>selected</code>, <code>loading</code>, <code>read</code>, <code>locked</code>).</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">Operation</td><td>Stable action identity (<code>open-article</code>, <code>save</code>, <code>request-access</code>) shared by UI, API, and agents — one operation, many actors.</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <p>Expression is separate and <em>granted</em>: Visual Language → Theme → Recipe, resolved through a <strong>pure, deterministic 12-layer cascade</strong> that leaves a per-field trace (source layer, prior value, resulting value, permitting contract clause, merge rule). Failure is closed: an unknown token, unknown asset, undeclared transform, or ambiguous conflict is a typed hard failure — never a silent default.</p>
  <p>Each rendering surface holds a <strong>Projection Contract</strong> — <code>preserve / transform / mayOmit / mayIntroduce</code> plus six invariance dimensions (<code>semantic, behavioral, actionIdentity, structural, morphological, visual</code>), each set to <code>required | bounded | free</code>. Protected fields — identity, required content types, semantic roles, operation identity, contract invariance levels, routing intent — are never overridable by any layer, including accessibility overrides and user style options.</p>
  <div class="law"><p>Two renderings of the same content are equivalent iff identities, required content and priority, operation identity, exposure and reachability, accessible names, roles and order, and responsive reachability all match. Pixel equality is explicitly not required.</p><span class="who">SES projection equivalence — the definition of “the same page in two themes”</span></div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 5 ============================ -->
<section id="s5">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">5</span><h2>The write path</h2></div>
  <p><strong>No persistent mutation executes outside a registered contract.</strong> Contract definitions are versioned records (<code>content.revise@1.0</code>, <code>content.promote@1.0</code>, <code>entitlement.grant@1.0</code>, <code>schema.migrate@1.0</code>); executions are instances moving through the ICP canonical lifecycle (<code>declared → ready → started → validating → … → completed | blocked | conflicted</code>). <code>blocked</code> is not <code>error</code>: every blocking outcome carries an executable recovery action (<code>refresh_record</code>, <code>review_conflict</code>, <code>reauthenticate</code>, <code>provide_proof</code>…) or a declared terminal reason.</p>
  <p>Verification level is <strong>derived from consequence, not UI preference</strong>:</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Effect class</th><th>Example</th><th>Verification</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">E0 · observational</td><td>read, subscribe</td><td class="mono">none</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">E1 · reversible draft</td><td>keystrokes, block reorder in draft</td><td class="mono">none — batched, receipted per session</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">E2 · compensable</td><td>unpublish, cache purge</td><td class="mono">confirm</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">E3 · consequential external</td><td>publish, entitlement change, price/legal content</td><td class="mono">confirm → reauthenticate</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">E4 · durable / irreversible</td><td>revocation with takedown obligations</td><td class="mono">prove</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <p>Every landed mutation produces a <strong>change receipt</strong> — actor, resource, before/after revision, path-level changes, evidence ids, verification id, reversibility class, compensation interaction, integrity digest — hash-chained into the append-only ledger.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 6 ============================ -->
<section id="s6">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">6</span><h2>The publish path</h2></div>
  <p>Publishing decomposes into two gates that must not collapse:</p>
  <ol>
    <li><strong>Qualification (EQP):</strong> given this exact revision, this exact claim set, this exact context — is the required evidence present, valid, current, and sufficient? Evidence results keep <code>PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL / INCONCLUSIVE / BLOCKED / NOT_RUN</code> distinct; missing evidence yields <code>inconclusive</code>, never pass.</li>
    <li><strong>Promotion:</strong> a separate E3 contract executed by a named authority. <code>QUALIFIED</code> does not mean live. Embargo is promotion with a declared world-time trigger.</li>
  </ol>
  <p>Re-qualification is incremental — the realtime publish equation:</p>
  <pre>RequiredEvidence(rev<span class="a">ₙ</span>) = InvalidatedEvidence(rev<span class="a">ₙ₋₁</span> → rev<span class="a">ₙ</span>)
                     + EvidenceForNewClaims(rev<span class="a">ₙ</span>)
                     + MandatoryProfileEvidence</pre>
  <p>Scope follows the qualification radius: a typo is <strong>R1</strong> (local); a slug change is <strong>R2</strong> (references and redirects re-verify); a content-type schema change is <strong>R3</strong> (every instance re-validates); shared-vocabulary changes are <strong>R4</strong>. The editor watches obligations resolve <em>live</em> — “publishable, blocked on 2 obligations” is a realtime surface that updates as evidence runs.</p>

  <h3>6.1 <span class="sub">·</span> Consequence profiles — the stopping condition</h3>
  <p>The Formalism essay’s warning is honored in the schema itself: a specify→check loop with no exit condition is the formalist’s characteristic failure, so every content class declares its gate roster <em>and its end</em>.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Profile</th><th>Example</th><th>Required evidence</th><th>Explicitly not required</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">note</td><td>personal post, changelog entry</td><td>schema-valid · access declared</td><td>link checks, review, a11y audit beyond defaults</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">article</td><td>essay, feature</td><td>+ links resolve · media has alt text · relations valid</td><td>legal review, human comprehension evidence</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">commitment</td><td>pricing, legal, medical, promises to named recipients</td><td>+ entitlement declared · recipient contract present · reauthenticated promotion · second attestation</td><td>—</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <div class="law"><p>“No further gates” is a declared statement, not silence. A draft note must never be gated like a legal page; a legal page must never ship like a note.</p><span class="who">The formalist’s correction: the stopping condition is part of the specification</span></div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 7 ============================ -->
<section id="s7">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">7</span><h2>Projections</h2></div>
  <p>Every consumable artifact is a derived projection of Canon: HTML pages, feeds, search index, sitemaps, notifications, embeddings, OG images, and the <strong>agent corpus</strong> (<code>llms.txt</code> / <code>llms-full.txt</code> — compiled context whose validity is an aggregate source digest, repaired at the source and recompiled, never hand-edited). Three disciplines govern derivation:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Frozen snapshot, one-way materialization.</strong> Derivation runs against frozen state S₀, produces G₀, materializes S₁ = S₀ + G₀. Generated artifacts are invisible to their own producing pass — no fixed-point loops. Derived content (summaries, embeddings, cross-links) enters future passes only explicitly, as <code>derived</code> records.</li>
    <li><strong>Access projection before serialization.</strong> <code>project_for(access)</code> removes invisible members and dangling edges <em>before any handle exists</em>. Projection is subtractive with respect to power: it may hide, withhold, relabel, understate; it may never manufacture a capability or grant a permission. Internally, <code>exposed / hidden / unavailable</code> stay unmerged; outwardly, mapping hidden→absent for low-access viewers is a <em>declared omission</em> in that surface’s contract.</li>
    <li><strong>Fingerprint-scoped invalidation.</strong> Every derived artifact records fine-grained dependency edges on its <em>access-projected</em> inputs and receives a structural fingerprint independent of execution order. A change to a field a given projection could not observe produces <strong>no invalidation for it</strong> — simultaneously the correct caching model and a side-channel guarantee: invalidation timing cannot leak hidden edits.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Every projection stage is classified in a published <strong>transformation ledger</strong> — <code>lossless / lossy-disclosed / interpretive / unsupported</code> — with the <code>unsupported</code> transformations listed so the refusal is auditable. A renderer can compute nothing and still mislead; the ledger is how it proves it didn’t.</p>

  <h3>7.1 <span class="sub">·</span> Surface resolution <span class="sub">(adopted 2026-08-28 · SCMS-008)</span></h3>
  <p>Between access projection and expression sits the <strong>surface</strong>: <code>Resolve(D, P, Q, C, L, A, T) → ResolvedSurface</code> — purpose-bound semantic participation (eligibility, membership, grouping, semantic priority, operation exposure, trace, fingerprint) under the pinned <strong>Semantic Surface System</strong> (<code>sss:protocol/semantic-surface</code> v0.1.0). The governing separation: <code>CANON ≠ SURFACE ≠ EXPRESSION ≠ REPRESENTATION</code> — the surface says <em>what matters here and why</em>; SES says <em>how it may appear</em>. SPS’s evidence-resolved morphology decomposes accordingly: selection and evidence tone are surface semantics, the container form is an expression recipe over them. Surface resolution runs read-only inside the derive phase; access projection precedes candidacy; agent semantic slices (§11) are ResolvedSurfaces; eligibility outcomes <code>eligible/ineligible/unknown/withheld/unsupported</code> join §3.5’s non-collapsible vocabulary. Implemented and tested at <code>impl/surface-resolver</code> (11 vectors, including the hidden-state non-leak). Full treatment, with real resolver output: <a href="https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7f0f7cd1-9220-422c-a0db-e63c4383922a">The Surface Seam</a>.</p>
  <p style="font-size:13.5px;color:var(--muted)">Canonical sources for this subsection: bindings/PROJECT_BINDINGS.yaml and FORMAL_RESOURCE_MANIFEST.json (main); the equivalent DESIGN.md text is the <span class="mono">[SSS]</span> hunk awaiting disposition on PR #28.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 8 ============================ -->
<section id="s8">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">8</span><h2>Realtime machinery</h2></div>

  <h3>8.1 <span class="sub">·</span> The commit cycle</h3>
  <p>One one-way loop per commit wave — the frame-scheduler discipline applied to a CMS:</p>
  <figure>
    <div class="figwrap">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 940 210" role="img" aria-label="The six-phase commit cycle: ingest, freeze, derive, commit, notify, observe, with observations looping back as input to the next wave only.">
      <defs>
        <marker id="arr2" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse">
          <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
        </marker>
      </defs>
      <g font-size="12.5" font-family="inherit">
        <g font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">
          <rect x="20"  y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="var(--accent)" fill-opacity="0.1" stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="1.5"/>
          <text x="80" y="80" fill="var(--accent-ink)">ingest</text>
          <rect x="176" y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/>
          <text x="236" y="80">freeze S₀</text>
          <rect x="332" y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/>
          <text x="392" y="80">derive</text>
          <rect x="488" y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/>
          <text x="548" y="80">commit S₁</text>
          <rect x="644" y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/>
          <text x="704" y="80">notify</text>
          <rect x="800" y="52" width="120" height="46" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/>
          <text x="860" y="80">observe</text>
        </g>
        <line x1="140" y1="75" x2="172" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <line x1="296" y1="75" x2="328" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <line x1="452" y1="75" x2="484" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <line x1="608" y1="75" x2="640" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <line x1="764" y1="75" x2="796" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <!-- phase notes -->
        <g font-size="10.5" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">
          <text x="80" y="116">contracts land</text>
          <text x="80" y="129">revisions + receipts</text>
          <text x="236" y="116">snapshot of Canon</text>
          <text x="236" y="129">for this wave</text>
          <text x="392" y="116">pure resolvers</text>
          <text x="392" y="129">against S₀ only</text>
          <text x="548" y="116">projection versions</text>
          <text x="548" y="129">recorded as derived</text>
          <text x="704" y="116">fingerprint invalidations</text>
          <text x="704" y="129">fan out through lenses</text>
          <text x="860" y="116">acks + manifests return</text>
          <text x="860" y="129">as observed records</text>
        </g>
        <!-- loop back -->
        <path d="M 860 98 L 860 172 L 80 172 L 80 102" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="5 4" marker-end="url(#arr2)"/>
        <text x="470" y="163" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="var(--muted)">next wave only — derived output and observations never feed the pass that produced them</text>
      </g>
    </svg>
    </div>
    <figcaption><strong>No phase reads what a later phase writes.</strong> The dashed return edge is the only feedback, and it crosses a wave boundary — the staging rule that excludes fixed-point loops, applied to content derivation.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <h3>8.2 <span class="sub">·</span> Subscriptions are lenses</h3>
  <p>A subscription is a declarative <strong>allow-list</strong> scope — records, metrics, relationship types, a radius around a subject — composed with the subscriber’s access projection. A lens narrows; it can never widen power. The wire format is the envelope itself: provenance travels with every message, and clients are bound by the no-promotion rule — an <code>observed</code> push can update a chip; it cannot overwrite a <code>declared</code> field in the local model.</p>

  <h3>8.3 <span class="sub">·</span> Invalidation, not state push</h3>
  <p>Readers hold a <strong>committed snapshot baseline</strong> — server-rendered truth, no-JS truth, deterministic builds. The notify phase pushes invalidation keys; clients re-fetch through access projection. If the live channel fails, the client silently keeps its snapshot and says so: failure degrades to truth, not to a spinner. Every live surface carries a <strong>provenance chip</strong> — the visible end of the consistency state machine:</p>
  <div class="chip-row" role="img" aria-label="Provenance chip states: live checked 4 seconds ago; snapshot from August 27; 2 revisions since snapshot; local unsent; conflicted, review.">
    <span class="chip live"><span class="dot"></span>live · checked 4s ago</span>
    <span class="chip"><span class="dot"></span>snapshot · Aug 27</span>
    <span class="chip stale"><span class="dot"></span>+2 revisions since snapshot</span>
    <span class="chip stale"><span class="dot"></span>local · unsent</span>
    <span class="chip conflict"><span class="dot"></span>conflicted — review</span>
  </div>
  <p class="chip-cap">A page that can prove it is not lying is a feature, not a caveat.</p>

  <h3>8.4 <span class="sub">·</span> Presence is observation</h3>
  <p>Cursors, selections, “Zach is editing,” view counts, soft locks: all <code>observed</code> envelopes with mandatory <code>observed_at</code> + <code>expires_at</code>. The consequences fall out structurally rather than by cleanup jobs:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Soft locks self-release</strong> — an expired presence record may not drive decisions, so an abandoned lock cannot hold content hostage.</li>
    <li><strong>Ghost cursors are impossible by construction</strong> — an expired cursor is no longer authoritative for rendering.</li>
    <li>Presence history is retained after expiry for replay, never for authority.</li>
    <li><strong>Cadence honesty</strong> — presence at seconds, metrics at their real rate, daily aggregates once per visit. Polling a daily aggregate is theater, and the surfaces say so.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3>8.5 <span class="sub">·</span> Concurrency discipline is derived from invariance</h3>
  <p>The synthesis at the center of R1: the same typed invariance that governs what a <em>theme</em> may change governs what <em>concurrent editors</em> may merge. One declaration, two enforcement surfaces.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Field invariance</th><th>Projection meaning</th><th>Concurrency discipline</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="keyw"><code>free</code><br><span class="mono" style="font-weight:400;color:var(--muted)">visual · morphological · prose body</span></td><td>themes may restyle freely</td><td>CRDT/OT merge; concurrent edits combine; E1, no ceremony</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="keyw"><code>bounded</code><br><span class="mono" style="font-weight:400;color:var(--muted)">block order · slot membership · socket population</span></td><td>themes may rearrange within declared bounds</td><td>merge, then validate against admission and cardinality invariants; violation → <code>conflicted</code>, surfaced — never a silent fallback winner</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="keyw"><code>required</code><br><span class="mono" style="font-weight:400;color:var(--muted)">identity · operations · entitlement · schema refs · routing</span></td><td>no surface may alter</td><td>serialized through a contract; the second concurrent attempt receives outcome <code>conflict</code> + executable recovery</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <div class="law"><p>Silent merge is a granted behavior — granted exactly where meaning is not at stake.</p><span class="who">SES typed invariance, applied to collaboration</span></div>

  <h3>8.6 <span class="sub">·</span> Consistency states</h3>
  <p>Each client’s relationship to each record is one of six HCML states, and the state — not optimism — decides what is permitted:</p>
  <figure>
    <div class="figwrap">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 940 270" role="img" aria-label="Consistency state machine: Current transitions to Stale-but-safe when a remote commit is observed; converging returns it to Current; overlap on a required field moves it to Conflicted, where publishing freezes but drafting continues; contract resolution returns to Current.       <defs>
        <marker id="arr3" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse">

      </defs>
      <g font-size="12.5" font-family="inherit">

    <figcaption><strong>The load-bearing asymmetry:</strong> conflict freezes <em>consequential</em> action while drafting continues. A CMS that blocks typing on conflict is unusable; one that publishes through conflict is lying.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <h3>8.7 <span class="sub">·</span> Events are edges, not a firehose</h3>
  <p>Live signals cross thresholds hysteretically (enter at 0.6, exit at 0.2) and emit one clean edge per crossing: <code>content:trending</code>, <code>content:staleness-warning</code>, <code>presence:entered / left</code>, <code>qualification:blocked / cleared</code>, <code>delivery:drifted / synchronized</code>. Subscribers receive transitions, not ticks.</p>

  <h3>8.8 <span class="sub">·</span> Degradation is governed and asymmetric</h3>
  <p>Under load, a quality governor sheds <em>cadence</em>, never <em>correctness</em>: projection refresh and notification frequency step down quickly (a few over-budget waves) and recover slowly (a sustained run of clean ones). The contract, qualification, and receipt planes never degrade. Degraded state is itself an observed record — visible on the chip, honest on the status page.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 9 ============================ -->
<section id="s9">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">9</span><h2>The field plane</h2></div>
  <p>The workspace is a Fundamental field in which records are bodies (identity doctrine <code>id / namespace / kind / host</code>) and typed relations are edges with fast <code>strength</code> and slow <code>memory</code>. Meaning maps to measurable channels:</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Meaning</th><th>Channel</th><th>Editorial reading</th></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">importance · priority</td><td class="mono">attention</td><td>what deserves presence now</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">urgency · recency</td><td class="mono">heat</td><td>what is hot, what is cooling</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">confidence</td><td class="mono">coherence</td><td>how settled a claim is</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">uncertainty</td><td class="mono">entropy</td><td>where disorder is accumulating</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">relationship · history</td><td class="mono">memory</td><td>worn paths, long-lived links</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">status</td><td class="mono">phase</td><td>draft gas → published solid</td></tr>
    <tr><td class="key">hierarchy</td><td class="mono">pressure</td><td>rank and depth</td></tr>
  </table></div>
  <p><strong>Metric provenance is typed.</strong> <code>computed</code> lanes the engine writes (attention, recency, staleness); <code>supplied-only</code> lanes only a human may set — <code>confidence</code> is never inferred (<em>a citation is not certainty</em>) and <code>risk</code> is never defaulted to zero (<em>“no risk” is a claim, not a safe blank</em>); <code>designed</code> lanes a pattern references must be supplied or they are flagged inert by lint.</p>
  <p><strong>Workspace morphology is resolved, not templated</strong> — SPS’s contribution. Each shelf of the editorial UI declares <code>{ purpose, lens, form }</code>, and its container (<code>hero / banner / rail / split / matrix / portals</code>) resolves from semantic purpose <em>plus evidence density</em>, with an evidence tone — <code>earned / steady / fading</code> — reflecting how many records actually satisfy the lens. The layout is a function of how much evidence supports the grouping. There is no generic dashboard shell.</p>
  <p><strong>Editorial time is five separate senses.</strong> Simulation time ticks (the field); host time is supplied (the platform); world time is declared (<code>publishedAt</code>, embargo instants — declaration beats inference); semantic time is derived (freshness half-lives per content class, imminence ramps toward embargo horizons, retention curves for archives); replay time is reconstructed (audit).</p>
  <div class="law"><p>Analytics claims sit on the causality ladder — observed → attributed → explained → replayed → predicted — and every surface quotes the highest level its data supports, and no higher.</p><span class="who">“Attention 0.8” is observed. “Readers love this” requires human evidence.</span></div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 10 ============================ -->
<section id="s10">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">10</span><h2>Access &amp; delivery honesty</h2></div>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Discovery without exposure.</strong> Entitlement-gated content participates in search, relations, and field signals through geometry, metadata, and observations — the text layer is a protected resource behind a <code>staged-access-request</code> state and an entitlement contract.</li>
    <li><strong>Delivery is observed; drift is explicit.</strong> Topology records declare what each edge and channel <em>should</em> serve; observed manifests report what each <em>does</em> serve. Divergence is <code>ObservationStatus: Drifted</code> with an explicit <code>differences[]</code> list — driving purge contracts, and shown honestly on status surfaces.</li>
    <li><strong>Gates must be able to fail.</strong> Every health check and CI gate has a declared trigger, a declared evidence requirement, and a demonstrable failure mode. A checker that crashes green, or a validator that no-ops outside its artifact class and exits 0, is a finding, not a gate. Validators report how many checks <em>actually ran</em>.</li>
    <li><strong>The wallpaper rule applies to the UI.</strong> Any surface that appears live must be derived from real state or declared as decoration — remedies in order: derive, declare, demote, sugar. Determinism is part of honesty: injected clocks, seeded randomness; an unseeded animation claiming to be a replay is a false claim.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 11 ============================ -->
<section id="s11">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">11</span><h2>Agents &amp; AI</h2></div>
  <p><strong>Read.</strong> Agents receive <em>semantic slices</em> — radius-bounded, access-filtered neighborhoods with provenance flags traveling with the slice — plus the <code>agent-json</code> projection surface and the compiled corpus. The read facade is safe by shape: there is nothing on it to call that mutates.</p>
  <p><strong>Write.</strong> Machine output enters as a <strong>Candidate</strong> and never self-promotes. An agent’s draft revision, suggested relation, or generated summary crosses the same EQP evidence and promotion authority as human work, and its provenance is visible for as long as the content lives.</p>
  <p><strong>Decide.</strong> High-uncertainty editorial decisions — takedowns, disputed corrections, taxonomy changes — may convene a PDP panel: consensus discounted by shared provenance (agreement counts once per independent axis), invalidation conditions pre-committed and asymmetric to pressure, and the human owning the weights, the stakes, and the exit. A model that flips under pressure has produced information about the model, not about the decision.</p>
  <p><strong>For whom.</strong> Content classes may require an RCP recipient record — a named person, their need in their framing, an obligation with a date. Status is derived, never assigned: <code>active / delivered / lapsed / primitive</code>. A lapsed recipient is retained, never deleted.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 12 ============================ -->
<section id="s12">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">12</span><h2>Versioning &amp; compatibility</h2></div>
  <p>Five version axes move independently: content identity · content-type schema · theme/visual language · resolver/pipeline · wire protocol. <strong>Equal version numbers imply nothing.</strong> Cross-axis compatibility is a declared conformance record over six dimensions — <code>syntax, schema, behavior, semantics, authority, evidence</code> — never inferred from matching numbers.</p>
  <p>Schema changes are classed — documentation / additive / conformance-tightening / breaking-semantic / breaking-expression / deprecation — each with required review. Deprecated semantic identities remain resolvable through a declared compatibility window, and a breaking-semantic migration is a qualification event at radius R3+ with its own evidence.</p>

  <h3>12.1 <span class="sub">·</span> Dependency doctrine <span class="sub">(owner directive, 2026-08-28)</span></h3>
  <p>The system is built <strong>in isolation</strong>. Formal resources and capabilities — SES, SPS, ICP, EQP, IEPE, HCML, Fundamental Engine, rr-rsp, and any reference system later accepted — are consumed <strong>as dependencies</strong>: pinned by version and revision/digest in the resource manifest, imported through declared bindings, never absorbed into this codebase.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Consumption mechanisms</strong> (whichever fits the artifact): a package/crate dependency, a schema-pack import, or a mechanical sync from a pinned upstream revision. A synced copy is a cache of the pin, not a fork.</li>
    <li><strong>Upstream-first repair.</strong> When a capability is needed, broken, or missing in a dependency, the change is made <em>in the owning project</em>, under that project's own authority and process; this project then re-pins the new revision. Local modification of consumed code or specs is prohibited.</li>
    <li><strong>Divergence is a deviation</strong> — typed, owner-authorized, bounded, visible, with the upstream fix landing as its reversal trigger. Never a silent patch.</li>
    <li><strong>A re-pin is a compatibility event</strong>: it carries a declared compatibility statement and may trigger re-qualification at the appropriate radius.</li>
    <li>Worked example: SES ships no package manifest today. If the implementation needs SES as an installable dependency, packaging is added upstream in <code>semantic-expression-system</code> and pulled — not vendored ad hoc here.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 13 ============================ -->
<section id="s13">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">13</span><h2>Reference implementation <span class="sub">(non-normative)</span></h2></div>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Store:</strong> Postgres. Revision and receipt tables append-only <em>by grant</em> — the runtime role has no UPDATE or DELETE. Logical decoding feeds the notify phase.</li>
    <li><strong>Resolver:</strong> one pure TypeScript library (no ambient time, no I/O) shared by server, edge, and client — the same cascade everywhere, held to golden conformance vectors, including a negative vector proving the gate can fail.</li>
    <li><strong>Wire:</strong> WebSocket lenses with SSE fallback; JSON envelopes; JCS canonicalization for hashing; Ed25519 attestation on promoted projections, with verification keys distributed out-of-band — a key carried alongside untrusted content only authenticates the attacker to itself.</li>
    <li><strong>Editor:</strong> CRDT (e.g. Yjs) strictly for invariance-<code>free</code> fields; <code>bounded</code> and <code>required</code> fields go through contract RPC. Presence over the observation channel with short expiries.</li>
    <li><strong>Edge:</strong> projection versions in KV; edges report served-version manifests back as observations; drift drives purge contracts.</li>
    <li><strong>The project itself</strong> bootstraps under formal-project-bootstrap v0.5.0: <code>PROJECT_INTENT.md</code>, <code>PROJECT_PROFILE.json</code>, a pinned formal-resource manifest (SES, SPS, ICP, EQP, IEPE-001, HCML, Fundamental, rr-rsp — by revision digest), <code>records/*.jsonl</code>, compiled context, and CI gates that demonstrably fail.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 14 ============================ -->
<section id="s14">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">14</span><h2>Narrowest end-to-end path</h2></div>
  <p>The first milestone, expressed as exit evidence rather than features:</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Canon holds one content type (<strong>Article</strong>: title/media/body/meta slots) and one composition (<strong>Home</strong>: hero + rail sockets) as Schema records.</li>
    <li><code>content.revise@1</code> lands draft revisions with session receipts.</li>
    <li>Two editors draft live: body text merges (<code>free</code>), block reorder validates (<code>bounded</code>), a slug conflict freezes publish (<code>required</code>) — <strong>R1 demonstrated</strong>.</li>
    <li>The qualification panel resolves the <strong>note</strong> profile’s obligations as evidence runs — the incremental RequiredEvidence equation, observable.</li>
    <li><code>content.promote@1</code> executes with confirm verification, producing a receipt and an attested projection version.</li>
    <li>The reader page renders from renderer-neutral output under <strong>two themes</strong>, passing projection-equivalence vectors — identical semantics, radically different pixels.</li>
    <li>The provenance chip cycles <code>snapshot → live → stale → live</code> under induced channel failure — <strong>R3 demonstrated</strong>.</li>
    <li>An edit to an entitlement-hidden field produces <strong>no invalidation on the public lens</strong> — cache correctness and non-leakage in one test.</li>
    <li>The <code>llms.txt</code> corpus projection regenerates deterministically, diff-gated in CI.</li>
  </ol>
</section>

<!-- ============================ 15 ============================ -->
<section id="s15">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">15</span><h2>Traceability</h2></div>
  <p>Every load-bearing element of this design binds to a concept already established in the source corpus. Nothing here mints a new primitive that could instead be referenced, bound, specialized, or composed.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>Design element</th><th>Concept</th><th>Source</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Envelope, provenance lattice, no-promotion rule</td><td>descriptor protocol</td><td class="mono">reflective-rust</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Four identity classes; hash ≠ compatibility</td><td>runtime identity doctrine</td><td class="mono">reflective-rust</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Append-only by grants; hash-chained ledger</td><td>custody in the database</td><td class="mono">PDP</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Multi-axis state; no single status enum</td><td>multi-dimensional maturity</td><td class="mono">CALP / bootstrap</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Slot/Block/Socket/Composition/Operation type system</td><td>semantic model</td><td class="mono">SES</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Projection Contracts; equivalence without pixels</td><td>expression governance</td><td class="mono">SES</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Pure 12-layer resolver; closed failure; field trace</td><td>resolution model</td><td class="mono">SES</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Contract-gated writes; receipts; blocked ≠ error</td><td>interaction lifecycle</td><td class="mono">ICP</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Qualification vs promotion; incremental evidence; radius</td><td>evidence discipline</td><td class="mono">EQP</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Consequence profiles as declared stopping condition</td><td>the formalist’s correction</td><td class="mono">Formalism</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Consistency states; conflict freezes consequence only</td><td>temporal consistency</td><td class="mono">HCML</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Candidates never self-promote; uncertainty retained</td><td>shared-state invariants</td><td class="mono">HCML / IEPE</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Records as bodies; meaning→metric; supplied-only lanes</td><td>semantic layers, metric provenance</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Association ≠ coupling; no haunted feeds</td><td>dimensional coupling</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Evidence-resolved morphology; no dashboard template</td><td>shelf resolver</td><td class="mono">SPS</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Provenance chips; snapshot-first; cadence honesty</td><td>live-data contract</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Hysteretic events; asymmetric degradation</td><td>event agent, quality governor</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Frozen-snapshot derivation; fingerprint invalidation</td><td>staging model, dependency tracking</td><td class="mono">reflective-rust</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Transformation ledger; absence vocabulary</td><td>the Observatory</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Discovery without text exposure; reader ≠ detail</td><td>publication boundaries</td><td class="mono">SPS</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Gates that can fail; validator applicability</td><td>register findings</td><td class="mono">Register / NPS</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Compiled agent corpus; digest validity</td><td>context compilation</td><td class="mono">IEPE / bootstrap</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Recipient contracts; derived status</td><td>RCP</td><td class="mono">Register</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Five senses of time; declaration beats inference</td><td>temporal model</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Causality ladder for analytics claims</td><td>causality and truth</td><td class="mono">Fundamental</td></tr>
  </table></div>
</section>

  <p><span class="mono">scms:design/semantic-cms · declared · project.owner · 2026-08-28</span></p>

This page is a derived projection; it preserves the design’s structure and claims, transforms prose into typographic and diagrammatic form, omits nothing normative, and introduces presentation only.</p>

<div class="shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">SCMS-002 · Review · semantic-cms</div>
  <h1>Titan &amp; Infinite-Verse Review</h1>
  <p class="standfirst">A comprehensive pass over two deep sibling systems — <strong>Titan/Chroma</strong>, a multi-product platform with a 32-runtime fleet, and <strong>Infinite-Verse</strong>, a semantic cultural knowledge platform — extracting what should inform the Semantic CMS. The six-plane design survives contact; two planes are missing; and sixteen amendments are proposed for owner disposition.</p>

  <div class="envelope" role="group" aria-label="This review, represented as a canonical record envelope">
    <div class="envelope-head">
      <span>Envelope · scms-0.1</span>
      <span class="seal">provenance: declared</span>
    </div>
    <div class="envelope-body">
      <table>
        <tr><td class="k">subject_id</td><td class="v">scms:review/titan-infinite-verse</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="k">work_item</td><td class="v">SCMS-002 · Done — proposals await owner disposition</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="k">source</td><td class="v">research/titan-infinite-verse-review.md · reviewed 2026-08-28</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="k">method</td><td class="v">four bounded exploration passes over compiled corpora + direct reads · single pass · observed, not adversarially verified</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="k">source_state</td><td class="v">Infinite-Verse 00e543c1 (dirty), 1 stale submodule (self-reported) · Titan VCS state not inspected</td></tr>
      </table>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="envelope-note">This page is a <em>derived</em> projection of the canonical review in the semantic-cms repository. DESIGN.md is deliberately unchanged — everything here is proposal, not amendment.</p>
</header>

<!-- ======================= 1 ======================= -->
<section id="s1">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">1</span><h2>The two systems</h2></div>
  <p><strong>Titan ("Chroma")</strong> is a multi-product platform — Snack, Book, FactoryAtlas, FleetMap, IP&nbsp;Navigator, IdentityBridge, Orchestration, Pipeline — over a shared fleet of 32 runtimes in 11 capability groups. Its doctrine inverts the usual question: not <em>who is this user?</em> but <em>what is allowed right now?</em> — collapse resistance, scoped authority, boundary-native architecture, temporal containment. Composition: <code>Product → Runtime → Contract → Broker → Provider → Receipt</code>, with "credential boundary = product boundary" and contracts as "the only allowed language between systems."</p>
  <p><strong>Infinite-Verse</strong> is a semantic cultural knowledge and experience platform: it "admits authorized physical and digital sources, resolves durable publication and corpus identity, records meaning with provenance and confidence, and powers integrated products through governed projections." Manga Verse is the first domain. It pins the same protocol suite this project pins, plus <strong>iPub</strong> — its immutable publication format over content-addressed bytes, with semantic envelopes attached by reference. It is, in effect, a sibling attempt at this project's thesis: an unusually well-specified contract corpus with a partial implementation.</p>
  <p><strong>Net relationship:</strong> Infinite-Verse confirms the design's spine and runs ahead of it on qualification and projection governance; Titan supplies the operational machinery — custody, realtime transport, observation, constitutional CI — that the design describes but does not yet specify. The Field plane is the one place the CMS design leads both.</p>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 2 ======================= -->
<section id="s2">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">2</span><h2>Verdict summary</h2></div>
  <div class="verdicts">
    <div class="verdict"><h4>The six-plane architecture survives contact</h4><p>Both systems independently converged on the same separations: append-only truth, governed writes, evidence-gated promotion, regenerable projections, disclosed observation. Nothing found contradicts the design's spine.</p></div>
    <div class="verdict"><h4>Two planes are missing</h4><p>Infinite-Verse demonstrates that <strong>Admission</strong> (what may enter, under what rights) and <strong>Entitlement</strong> (who may see what, at section granularity) are distinct planes — a CMS that skips them grows them accidentally, per-projection.</p></div>
    <div class="verdict"><h4>Qualification needs a fourth verdict column</h4><p>Both systems learned the same lesson: "could not run" and "never ran" must block promotion exactly like "failed" — and gates must be provably able to fail (vacuous-pass detection, evaluator self-tests).</p></div>
    <div class="verdict"><h4>Live co-authoring has a second lawful answer</h4><p>Titan's Generative Relationship Protocol shows divergence-first collaboration — permanent legal branches over an immutable DAG, merge as an explicit authored act — which composes with append-only Canon better than silent convergence.</p></div>
    <div class="verdict"><h4>Live propagation has a proven transport</h4><p>Transactional outbox → LISTEN/NOTIFY fanout → backfill-then-live → <code>last_event_id</code> replay → <code>lagged</code> disclosure. No new infrastructure, no event loss, staleness disclosed as protocol messages.</p></div>
    <div class="verdict"><h4>Live honesty is richer than the design knows</h4><p>Two-clock freshness with tracked skew, hysteresis on state transitions, presence announced not inferred, UNKNOWN rendered as its own state, and absence carrying a reason code.</p></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 3 ======================= -->
<section id="s3">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">3</span><h2>Plane-by-plane findings</h2></div>
  <div class="legend">
    <span><span class="tag c">C</span>confirms the design</span>
    <span><span class="tag b">B</span>better mechanism than the design specifies</span>
    <span><span class="tag n">N</span>novel, applicable</span>
    <span><span class="tag g">G</span>generative, not directly applicable</span>
  </div>

  <h3><span class="tag n">N</span>Plane 0 — Admission (missing from the design)</h3>
  <p>Infinite-Verse records, for every source intake: custody, a <strong>set</strong> of permitted operations (<code>inspect · normalize · ingest · enrich · train · redistribute</code> — "a physical purchase does not automatically authorize digitization, model training, or redistribution"), rights scope, retention, and identity disposition. Four outcomes, including <strong><code>metadata-only</code></strong> — a source that participates in discovery with zero byte-processing authority. The ingestion rule: <em>"a file becomes a publication in one transaction; it becomes comprehended afterwards, asynchronously, and never blocks becoming readable."</em></p>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag b">B</span>Canon</h3>
  <p><strong>Confirmed:</strong> append-only enforced in the store (triggers, grant-less roles, "no UPDATE or DELETE paths"); JCS→SHA-256 content identity; supersession lineage; hash-linked receipts.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Teaching triggers</strong> — the append-only trigger's exception message states the correct procedure ("re-project into a new revision under a newer ruleset_version"). Enforcement that educates.</li>
    <li><strong>Identity is minted, never derived.</strong> A per-job mint ledger makes retried commits idempotent while new jobs mint fresh identity for identical bytes; an <code>identity_scheme</code> column with <em>no DEFAULT</em> ("a default would silently label a row nobody classified"). Its inverse discipline in GRP: <strong>hash-input selection as a design act</strong> — IDs exclude timestamps and model output so retries converge. Shared rule: <em>nothing derived from a detector or model output is identity-stable across versions.</em></li>
    <li><strong>Idempotency conflict detection</strong> — same key + same payload → dedup; same key + <em>different</em> payload → 422. "Prevents silent corruption."</li>
    <li><strong>Transactional outbox</strong> — the domain write and its event row commit in one transaction; audit INSERT shares the transaction with the state UPDATE, so an optimistic-lock failure rolls back both.</li>
    <li><strong>Vocabulary version witnesses</strong> on every row (<code>ruleset_version</code>, <code>parser_or_model_version</code>…) — "which rows predate the fix?" becomes a query, not archaeology.</li>
    <li><strong>Migrations as design records</strong> — 312-line migrations that are ~70% argument, including "What this migration deliberately does NOT do."</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag b">B</span>Contracts</h3>
  <p><strong>Confirmed:</strong> single write door; typed outcomes; executable recovery; optimistic concurrency where the 409 carries what you need to converge (<code>expected_base_digest</code>; the legal next-state list).</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>The fourth custody clause:</strong> every component declares <em>owns / may consume / may issue / <strong>must never become</strong></em>, with <code>forbidden_reads</code>/<code>forbidden_writes</code> — and the declarations are <strong>derived from the actual route surface</strong> by tooling, flagged for human confirmation. The named failure set: "coordinator → hidden user graph, broker → credential sink, runtime → tenant state holder, provider → identity authority, client → trusted state source."</li>
    <li><strong>Constitutional CI:</strong> doctrine compiled into greps — "must not persist memory" enforced by grepping for ORM imports; illegal-states tables (illegal state → prevention mechanism → status → evidence).</li>
    <li><strong>"Absent ≠ false"</strong> as a written consumer rule: additive-only contract versioning where absent fields mean <em>not declared</em>, never a positive assertion — plus an explicit <code>connections_declared</code> "I haven't told you" flag.</li>
    <li><strong>PATCH tri-state:</strong> absent key ≠ explicit <code>null</code> ≠ <code>{}</code> — assembled key-by-key because a spread collapses them.</li>
    <li><strong>Client pre-flight three-law:</strong> never looser than the server, never masks a server decision, counts code points — stricter-only is the one direction contracts may deviate.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag b">B</span><span class="tag n">N</span>Qualification</h3>
  <p><strong>Confirmed:</strong> qualification ≠ promotion — Infinite-Verse attestations carry <code>qualificationAuthority: "qualify-deployment.py"</code> with <code>promotionAuthority: null</code>, structurally separated, with mandatory <code>limitations[]</code>.</p>
  <div class="law"><p>Promotion over partial coverage asserts more than was established. Full coverage or no promotion — "could not run" and "never ran" block exactly like "failed."</p><span class="who">Infinite-Verse promote-staging.py · the four-column verdict</span></div>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>The vacuous-pass gate:</strong> run every evaluator against a populated corpus and an empty one; a gate that can observe absence must not return green on the empty one. Behavioral, not syntactic. Measured impact: <strong>22 phantom passes</strong> before it existed. Half the gate roster ships a self-test twin proving it can fail.</li>
    <li><strong>Delivery-time qualification</strong> (Titan Book): every citation in a generated response must resolve into the exact evidence set retrieved <em>for this request</em>; one unresolvable citation blocks the whole artifact — never partial. The adversarial challenger is <em>non-blocking</em>. And the <strong>decision is fingerprinted</strong>, not just the artifact — over <code>(namespace, policy_version, outcome, attempts, verified_ids)</code> — so a block is as auditable as a publish, and a policy change provably changes the fingerprint.</li>
    <li><strong>Two-tier materiality:</strong> machine attachments are non-material (re-detection mints no revision); human-verified work may be <em>promoted to material</em>, which mints a revision — "making editorial work part of publication identity."</li>
    <li><strong>Freshness as an obligation field:</strong> each obligation names its own invalidation event ("a redeploy invalidates it"). And <strong>qualify what is served</strong>, not what is configured — "config is not the artifact."</li>
    <li><strong>Content-safe promotion:</strong> "Ancestry lies" — compare content trees, not commit graphs. A promotion-lock race exits <em>could-not-verify</em>, never <em>refused</em>.</li>
    <li><strong>Prose gates:</strong> claim-reconciliation tables (✅/⚠️/❌/❓ per public claim, "anything not ✅ should not appear in copy") and the <strong>operational promise register</strong> — promises with no code identifier extracted into a machine-checked register, because "verifiable claims fail loudly; promises fail silently."</li>
    <li><strong>Fabrication lint:</strong> "absent stays absent" — no invented defaults; a guess must be declared as a diagnostic. "This gate is the memory" of five hand-removed fabrications.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag b">B</span>Projection</h3>
  <p><strong>Confirmed:</strong> stored-vs-derived doctrine stated identically in both systems — "Measured, with provenance and confidence" vs "Regenerable. Never written back into the publication." Six-dimension projection profiles running in production registries. "The UI never reads tables. It requests a view."</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong><code>computed_from</code> lineage:</strong> every projection row carries the digest-set it was computed from; <em>stale</em> is a join against append-only invalidation records; never-computed ≠ stale; stale-while-revalidate only if the marker stays visible. Composes with the design's fingerprint invalidation: fingerprints propagate invalidity, <code>computed_from</code> makes staleness <em>queryable</em>.</li>
    <li><strong>Declared refresh policy per projection</strong> — eager (writer pays) / lazy-on-read (first reader pays) / scheduled (batch pays), lazy by default — and <strong>human-verification eagerness overrides every policy</strong>: "a human corrects a speaker attribution and the search document still serving the machine's guess an hour later squanders exactly the authority the two-tier model exists to protect."</li>
    <li><strong>Supersession declared, never inferred</strong> — same scope, same detector class, explicit lineage; "timestamps must not be used to guess an ordering"; human documents never superseded by machine re-runs. <strong>Multiplicity is the default</strong> — disagreement stays visible.</li>
    <li><strong>One merge function</strong> for reader and owner, with access as a parameter — "so a reader and an owner can never see two different merges of the same documents."</li>
    <li><strong>Derivative classes, not encodings</strong> — manifests declare <code>thumbnail / preview / reader-medium / reader-large</code>; codecs live downstream so re-encoding can't change content identity.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag n">N</span>Field — the design leads; two additions</h3>
  <p>Both systems know <em>what</em> to measure (eight normalized page dimensions; a typed signals taxonomy) but neither has a live field — the design's Fundamental-based plane leads. Two additions:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>The Library Substrate canvas</strong> is the Field plane's missing evidence layer, already working: 10 z-normalized dimensions, k-means shelves with cohesion, an <strong>evidence floor as a live, unit-labeled control</strong>, and <strong>name qualification</strong> — a curated shelf name applies only when its signature matches <em>and</em> cohesion clears 0.55; otherwise the refusal is rendered with the actual and required numbers and the cluster keeps its machine description ("negative space +1.42σ · dialogue density −0.88σ"). A standing <strong>expectation harness</strong> — "N of 12 assertions hold" — runs tests of <em>meaning</em> over live data. Observations are <strong>revision-scoped with named confounds</strong>: the same work measures differently per edition; "ink coverage must be normalised per revision before clustering."</li>
    <li><strong>Signals governance</strong> (Titan): server-truth vs client-reported (advisory only) vs derived metrics with <strong>mandatory TTLs</strong> ("permanent behavioral histories are forbidden") — and a <strong>deliberately lossy boundary</strong>: only a coarse verdict crosses out of the Field, never a rich profile; the Field "does not know handles exist." Plus per-field <strong>truth types</strong> (<code>semantic / canonical / operational / abstain</code>) driving both retrieval and re-derivation policy.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag c">C</span><span class="tag b">B</span><span class="tag n">N</span>Observation</h3>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Presence and transport are two axes</strong> — <code>HOT/ACTIVE/IDLE/STALE/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN</code> × <code>HEALTHY/DEGRADED/UNHEALTHY/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN</code> — with UNKNOWN <em>rendered</em>, not blank: "we don't know" ≠ "not here."</li>
    <li><strong>Two-clock freshness:</strong> staleness computed against server-issued time with tracked skew — "every 'updated 3s ago' badge you'd otherwise ship is a lie on a skewed client."</li>
    <li><strong>Presence is announced, not inferred:</strong> a runtime that starts healthy and never transitions is invisible — "'missing' and 'healthy' look identical" (measured: 23 configured, 1 event seen). Heartbeats fire on <em>edges</em> with auto-composed numeric reasons; <code>Degraded</code> is a serving state distinct from <code>Down</code>.</li>
    <li><strong>Disclosed subscriber staleness:</strong> the event stream emits <code>lagged</code> when a subscriber falls behind — staleness as a protocol message, with catch-up-then-live as the canonical consumer shape.</li>
    <li><strong>Absence with a reason code:</strong> every scalar is <code>{value, source, confidence, absent_reason}</code> (<code>NO_STORE / NO_WRITER / NOT_CAPTURED</code>); off-ladder observations render <code>(off-ladder)</code> and sort last, visibly. Three absence granularities — <code>empty</code> / <code>absent</code> / <code>error</code> — never merged; named-absence routes stay deep-linkable with <code>declared: false</code> distinguishable from designed absence.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3><span class="tag n">N</span>Entitlement — underspecified in the design</h3>
  <p>Infinite-Verse treats entitlement as its own model, twice: <strong>section-level access classes</strong> — every semantic section is <code>open</code> (geometry, metrics, relation topology: "what shelves and similarity run on") or <code>entitled</code> (all text layers, anything "precise enough to reconstruct narrative"), enforced by one shared restriction function "so this route cannot become a second, laxer definition of what open means" — and the <strong>five-record independence rule</strong>: <code>ProviderAssertion ≠ ProviderTransaction ≠ EntitlementClaim ≠ EntitlementProjection ≠ LibraryEntry</code>, evidence flowing one way, claims never destructively merged, projections recomputable-from-claims with a fixture-replay gate. Plus <strong>404-not-403</strong>: absence copy must not confirm existence to someone probing.</p>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 4 ======================= -->
<section id="s4">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">4</span><h2>The realtime obligations, revisited</h2></div>

  <h3>R1 — live co-authoring</h3>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>The divergence-first lane.</strong> Neither system uses CRDTs anywhere. GRP's answer — immutable typed nodes, 23 edge types, paths as projections over the DAG, sibling branches structurally invisible to each other, and <strong>merge as an explicit authored act</strong> in five modes (<code>synthesize / replace / augment / overlay / compare_then_merge</code>, with overlay "preserving each voice") — composes with append-only Canon in a way silent convergence cannot. Its <strong>traversable-relationship whitelist</strong> (only 6 of 23 edge types carry context; <code>contradicts</code> is recorded but does not propagate) separates edge <em>semantics</em> from edge <em>reachability</em>. Proposal: CRDT stays for micro-convergence inside a draft's free fields; branch/authored-merge handles document-scale divergence.</li>
    <li><strong><code>changeCertainty</code>.</strong> Every write outcome carries <code>asserted / derived / indeterminate</code> alongside <code>changed</code> — and <code>indeterminate</code> must carry a retry bound to the <em>original</em> idempotency key. The difference between "your edit didn't save" and "we don't know whether it saved" — only the second has a safe remedy. Companion: <strong><code>receiptSurrogate</code></strong> — receipt-shaped responses that are not receipts travel under a different name, because "a client that constructs one has produced an audit record for an event it did not witness."</li>
    <li><strong>Rendered-set-bounded deletion.</strong> Deletes are authorized only for records the actor was actually shown; omitting the set means "shown nothing," so nothing may be deleted. Shipped-bug provenance: a diff against a fetched-but-unshown envelope turned one mark into 1 add + 20 deletes, reported as success. And on a stale reorder: deliberately <em>no "try again"</em> — re-sending would discard the other writer's work.</li>
  </ul>

  <h3>R2 — live propagation</h3>
  <div class="law"><p>Nothing happens without an emission. The audit log, the dashboard, the dead-letter queue, the SLA monitor, and downstream replicas are all subscribers to the same stream the system needed to emit for its own integrity.</p><span class="who">Titan Pipeline — the transport doctrine</span></div>
  <p>The proven shape: transactional outbox as the sole emission source → LISTEN/NOTIFY fanout (horizontal-safe, no new infrastructure) → scoped subscriptions → <strong>backfill-burst-then-live</strong> on connect → reconnect with <code>last_event_id</code> replayed from the outbox ("no event loss" as an acceptance criterion) → <code>lagged</code> overflow disclosure. The client seam is a <code>Stream&lt;T&gt;</code> contract that mocks drive with scripted frames, "so realtime code paths run for real long before a socket gateway exists."</p>

  <h3>R3 — live honesty</h3>
  <p>Two-clock freshness; hysteresis with instrumentation; announce-on-start; UNKNOWN rendered; <strong><code>mockIsSilent</code> as a defect class</strong> — mock data present without a URL-discoverable override ("a screenshot of mock content was verified as 'live mode'"); staleness disclosures on frozen exports; and the compiled-corpus header that names its own payload hash, dirty flags, and STALE INPUT banner — the pattern for this project's own compiled context.</p>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 5 ======================= -->
<section id="s5">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">5</span><h2>Cross-cutting governance</h2></div>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Gates provably able to fail, operationalized:</strong> vacuous-pass detection, self-test twins, gate-enumeration and invocation-coverage gates, and provenance stamps on every run — "a bare '29/29 full coverage' cannot be verified by anyone, including its author a day later."</li>
    <li><strong>Deviation register with escalation:</strong> violations are permitted <em>if filed</em> — blast radius, rotation, reversal trigger, owner — and an unfiled violation auto-escalates one severity level.</li>
    <li><strong>Assurance never aggregated:</strong> ten independent dimensions, generated from the registry so the table can't drift, with deliberately no score — "a percentage is how a table like this starts lying."</li>
    <li><strong>The spec-health register:</strong> a tagged list (<code>GUESS / GAP / THIN / CAVEAT</code>) of exactly where a spec forces a builder to invent — "listed so the invention becomes a decision instead."</li>
    <li><strong>Doc-vs-code drift typed:</strong> VIOLATION (code wrong) vs INACCURACY (docs wrong), with Built/Partial/Paper self-labels.</li>
    <li><strong>A naming collision to resolve deliberately:</strong> Titan's "planes" (Record/Event/Workflow/Policy/Retrieval) overlap but differ from this design's six — a bindings entry should align or explicitly diverge; silence would be drift.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 6 ======================= -->
<section id="s6">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">6</span><h2>Proposed amendments</h2></div>
  <p>Sixteen proposals, recorded for owner disposition — DESIGN.md is unchanged until you rule on them. Each names its source and target section.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table class="ledger">
    <tr><th>#</th><th>Amendment</th><th>Target</th><th>Source</th></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P1</span></td><td>Add an <strong>Admission plane</strong>: source-admission records with processing-authority sets, rights scope, retention, and the <code>metadata-only</code> outcome; comprehension asynchronous, never blocking readability</td><td class="mono">new §3.0</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P2</span></td><td>Specify <strong>Entitlement</strong>: section-level <code>open</code>/<code>entitled</code> classes with one shared restriction function; the five-record independence chain; 404-not-403</td><td class="mono">§10</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P3</span></td><td><strong>Four-column qualification verdicts</strong> — could-not-run and not-run block like failure; BLOCKED never collapses; vacuous-pass gate + self-tests required of every evaluator; freshness as per-obligation invalidation; qualify what is served</td><td class="mono">§6</td><td class="mono">IV · Titan</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P4</span></td><td><strong><code>computed_from</code> + declared refresh policy</strong> on every projection; human-verification eagerness override; supersession declared never inferred; multiplicity default</td><td class="mono">§7</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P5</span></td><td><strong>Two-tier materiality</strong>: machine attachments non-material; human promotion mints revisions</td><td class="mono">§3, §6</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P6</span></td><td>Custody declarations gain <strong>"must never become"</strong> + forbidden reads/writes/calls, derived from actual surfaces; constitutional CI (doctrine-as-greps, illegal-states table)</td><td class="mono">§2</td><td class="mono">Titan</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P7</span></td><td><strong>Divergence-first co-authoring lane</strong>: branch + authored merge (five modes) at document scale; traversable-edge whitelist; CRDT only for intra-draft free-field convergence</td><td class="mono">§8.5</td><td class="mono">Titan GRP</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P8</span></td><td><strong><code>changeCertainty</code></strong> (asserted/derived/indeterminate) on every write outcome + <strong><code>receiptSurrogate</code></strong> for receipt-shaped non-receipts</td><td class="mono">§5</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P9</span></td><td><strong>Rendered-set-bounded destructive operations</strong> — deletes authorized only against what the actor was shown</td><td class="mono">§8.5</td><td class="mono">IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P10</span></td><td><strong>Specify the R2 transport</strong>: transactional outbox as sole emission source; backfill-then-live; <code>last_event_id</code> replay; <code>lagged</code> disclosure; idempotency-conflict 422 on ingest</td><td class="mono">§8.1–8.3</td><td class="mono">Titan</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P11</span></td><td><strong>Extend Observation</strong>: presence × transport axes; UNKNOWN rendered; hysteresis; announce-on-start; two-clock freshness; <code>absent_reason</code> codes; three absence granularities; named-absence routes</td><td class="mono">§8.4, §8.6</td><td class="mono">Titan · IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P12</span></td><td><strong>Delivery-time qualification</strong> for generated/cited content: known-set citation gate (one failure blocks the artifact); non-blocking challenger; fingerprint the decision including policy version</td><td class="mono">§6, §11</td><td class="mono">Titan</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P13</span></td><td><strong>Field evidence governance</strong>: surfaced evidence floor; name qualification with rendered refusals; expectation harness; revision-scoped observations; metric TTLs; lossy verdict-only boundary; truth-type classification</td><td class="mono">§9</td><td class="mono">IV · Titan</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P14</span></td><td><strong>Identity discipline</strong>: mint ledger for retry-idempotent identity; scheme-version columns without DEFAULTs; documented hash-input selection; nothing detector-derived is identity-stable</td><td class="mono">§3.3</td><td class="mono">IV · GRP</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P15</span></td><td><strong>Prose gates</strong>: claim-reconciliation table + operational-promise register in CI; spec-health register beside DESIGN.md; deviation register with auto-escalation</td><td class="mono">§10, §13</td><td class="mono">Titan · IV</td></tr>
    <tr><td><span class="prop-id">P16</span></td><td><strong>Bindings entry</strong> resolving the Titan "plane" vocabulary collision — align or explicitly diverge</td><td class="mono">bindings</td><td class="mono">review §5</td></tr>
  </table></div>

  <h3>Candidate resource pins (also awaiting disposition)</h3>
  <p><code>titan-systems</code> (SYSTEMS_CONTRACT, custody doctrine, fleet-contract/tracker, grounding-gate, canonical-serializer, event-runtime protocol) · <code>infinite-verse</code> (iPub docs 03/17/18/19/20/21, source admission, ingest contract, entitlement model, EQP deployment profile, promotion scripts, key migrations) · <code>grp</code> (node/edge/path types, lineage traversal, merge modes). All as <code>kind: reference</code> — informing, not normative. Infinite-Verse is dirty at review time; pin after commit.</p>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 7 ======================= -->
<section id="s7">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">7</span><h2>Generative, not directly applicable</h2></div>
  <ul>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>Verified speculative decoding</strong> (FastBLT) — a cheap draft accepted only when an expensive verifier agrees, with proven baseline equivalence: the contract shape for optimistic local rendering with server verification. Its "Non-Claims" section is a doc pattern to steal regardless.</li>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>Eleven streaming renderers over one settling-tail model</strong> (<code>tokenProg</code>) — one progress abstraction, N presentation mappings: streaming visual style as a theme, not a rewrite.</li>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>The single-file offline projection</strong> — a whole app in one HTML file with a UUID→base64 manifest, blob rematerialization, and a strict direct-parent-only frame relay (root never sends upward, because <code>window.top</code> may be foreign) — a serious model for "export this space as one durable offline artifact," security model included, paired with an honest staleness disclosure when the export falls behind.</li>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>Trail decay as a freshness metaphor</strong> — recency rendered as literal visual fade.</li>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>Component contracts shipping their own prompt + specimen</strong> — every block type could carry its authoring prompt and a rendered specimen beside its schema.</li>
    <li><span class="tag g">G</span><strong>IP-as-content</strong> — patents with lifecycles, coverage-gap flags, and drift detection when architecture changes without IP review: a worked example of a commitment-class content type. And <strong>"no calendar promises in doctrine"</strong> — roadmap artifacts carry dependency order only.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<!-- ======================= 8 ======================= -->
<section id="s8">
  <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">8</span><h2>Maturity caveats</h2></div>
  <div class="law"><p>Addendum 9.1 — adversarially verified (SCMS-005): 6 claims confirmed, 4 partial, 0 refuted. Corrections: doc 19 and the entitlement model are <em>proposed</em> contracts, not ratified/enforced; GRP's timestamp exclusion fails on its operational fallback path; Snack's <code>last_event_id</code> replay is plan-only (shipped catch-up uses a timestamp cursor). No proposal invalidated; P2/P4/P10 dispositions should note source maturity. Full verdicts: records/evidence.jsonl · scms-evidence-005.</p><span class="who">Independent adversarial pass · 2026-08-28</span></div>
  <p>Both systems' own accounting bounds every claim above. <strong>Titan:</strong> the planes directory doesn't exist; 1 of 32 runtimes carries its mandatory authority doc; the SEC-* policy suite is referenced everywhere and exists nowhere; one safety gate "fails open." What survives its own reality check — and is safest to copy — is the code-backed set: fleet-contract/tracker, grounding-gate, canonical-serializer, event-runtime, the boundary checker, manifest generation. <strong>Infinite-Verse:</strong> its 26-gap implementation register is scrupulous — no <code>work</code> table, manifests not served, the manifest hash not yet a hash; "members of twenty-two implemented conformantly end-to-end: still none." Borrow on the strength of the reasoning, not on scale evidence. <strong>This review</strong> is a single pass, <code>observed</code>, not adversarially verified.</p>
</section>

The design specification lives in its own artifact; nothing in it changes until the proposals above are dispositioned.</p>
